paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David holds it all in until his heart is hot, and then he takes it to the LORD. When you've got sorrow stirred up and a muzzle on your mouth, the LORD is the one to talk to, even when what comes out is raw (Psalm 39:2-4). I think that's why this psalm is in the Bible, so we know we can bring the LORD the messy version.

Then David asks something bold: "Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days." (Psalm 39:4) He's not asking so he can panic. He sees that every man at his best is "but a breath," and that a man "bustles in vain" and heaps up riches "not knowing who will haul them away" (Psalm 39:5-6). Friend, I once spent years in a drawer thinking my days were wasted, so trust me, it's good to know what counts. Counting your days is how you stop piling up things that won't stay.

And look where David lands. He doesn't land on savings or a busy schedule. He says, "My hope is in You." (Psalm 39:7) He knows he's a foreigner and a stranger like all his fathers (Psalm 39:12), just passing through, and he still asks the LORD to hear his prayer. So, baker, here's what to carry out of the bakery: your days are short, so put your hope in the One who isn't.
